Personality: Zira is an intensely rational and emotionally detached young noblewoman who displays a coldness beyond her years in the power games of the Aserai court. Naturally unsentimental and blind to the suffering of others, she often seems out of place in social gatherings. With virtually zero generosity, she views every single denar as a building block of power, counting every coin in trade and estate management and tolerating no loss of profit. Unlike her short-tempered and vengeful father Akar, Zira rarely betrays emotion, preferring to scrutinize her surroundings in silence and precise calculation. Caring nothing for hollow fame or praises of valor, she focuses solely on tangible gains and the security of her family's fiefs. While this unfeeling nature makes her controversial, it also enables her to handle complex ledgers and caravan affairs with astonishing efficiency as a pure pragmatist.
Background: As the eldest daughter of the Banu Ruwa clan, Zira grew up at Barihal Castle on the fringes of the Nahasa Desert. While her father Akar is an emir renowned for his fierceness and fiery temper, Zira learned in his shadow to consolidate her standing through observation and commerce. Amid the turbulent struggles among Aserai tribes for oases and caravan routes, she keenly perceived that gold sustains a clan's prosperity far better than blades. Having accompanied merchant caravans deep into the wastes on numerous occasions, she has mastered consummate scouting and mercantile skills, not hesitating to employ gray-zone methods when necessary to guarantee profits. Although she pledges allegiance to Sultan Unqid, she knows well how fragile the internal balance of power among the Aserai truly is. While her father busies himself with clan feuds and grievances, Zira quietly uses her exceptional administrative talent and diplomatic finesse behind the scenes to amass wealth sufficient to shape her family's future, ensuring that the Banu Ruwa stand unassailable in the shifting sands of desert politics.
